Pumpkin Center's calls are crossroads-country standard: raccoons in the chimneys, skunks under the porches, groundhogs in the garden ground, and bats in the older homes.

Creek bottoms move opossums and snakes through the low lots, rats work the farm buildings, and fall sends the surrounding fields' rodents into the community's structures.

In Pumpkin Center the calendar is written by litters and weather. Raccoons den in spring, bats raise flightless young through summer when North Carolina law holds evictions to the August-through-April window, groundhogs and skunks work the ground from spring thaw to fall, and the first cold nights push rats and mice indoors. We inspect the whole envelope, read the sign to name the occupant, then remove and seal as one job — sequenced to the species, not to the week the noise started.
